title: Haar Moments and the Mathieu Property of Reductive Homogeneous Spaces
summary: Gives fixed-multiplier counterexamples and a classification for reductive homogeneous spaces, including disconnected acting groups.
verification: Written all-order proofs; limited exact polynomial and radial checks. Independent replay, formal verification and external review are not yet claimed.
next_steps: Obtain an independent mathematical review and replay the stated exact checks.
Resolve review findings and finalize submission metadata before depositing.
abstract:
We construct regular functions $P,Q$ on each of $\SL_2/2O$ and
$\SL_2/2I$ for which every positive Haar moment of $P$ vanishes, whereas
$\h(QP^m)$ is nonzero for infinitely many $m$. The same elementary
construction also supplies a radial witness on the defining module of
$\SU(2)$. These three examples give the following classification: for a
complex homogeneous space $G/H$, with $G$ and $H$ having reductive identity
components, the kernel of normalized Reynolds integration is
Mathieu--Zhao exactly when $[G^0,G^0]\subseteq H$. We give the reduction
to the examples, including disconnected acting groups. The counterexamples
are proved directly from Haar integration, polynomial identities and
Dirichlet's theorem. Every nonconstant polynomial recomposition of either
exceptional example has an explicit fixed multiplier whose ordinary
Cauchy transform is transcendental. Over an arbitrary coefficient algebra,
we also determine the pure and safe elements of the polynomial subalgebra
generated by the example.
